item.title: CVE-2026-99526 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
smb: client: fix use-after-free infoleak via the readdir resume name
CIFSFindNext() copies the resume name that cifs_save_resume_key() recorded from the last entry of the previous response into its request; psrch_inf->presume_name points into the response buffer that entry came from, and nothing ever clears it. find_cifs_entry() records a new name only from a response with a usable last entry, and cifs_readdir() only from an entry it walks to, so a response that carries no entries and leaves last_entry NULL, because CIFSFindFirst() or CIFSFindNext() rejected LastNameOffset, refreshes neither and presume_name keeps pointing into the previous response. That buffer has already been released: by CIFSFindNext() before it installs the new response, or by find_cifs_entry() when it rewinds the search, which does not drop the name either and can then fail in initiate_cifs_search() before a new response replaces it. The next CIFSFindNext() then copies up to PATH_MAX - 1 bytes of the resume name out of the released buffer into its request and sends them to the server: a use-after-free read that leaks kernel memory to a malicious or compromised server, which can provoke it with a single FindNext response that carries no entries and a LastNameOffset above CIFSMaxBufSize, which is all the existing check rejects.
With KASAN enabled, a server that answers a listing that way gives:
CIFS: VFS: ignoring corrupt resume name ================================================================== BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in CIFSFindNext+0x8ca/0x14c0 Read of size 4080 at addr ffff88807c823f98 by task ls/83
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 83 Comm: ls Tainted: G B 7.3.0-rc4-00457-gf14572c203d5 #69 PREEMPT(lazy) Tainted: [B]=BAD_PAGE Call Trace: <TASK> kasan_report+0xdf/0x1a0 kasan_check_range+0x10f/0x1e0 __asan_memcpy+0x23/0x60 CIFSFindNext+0x8ca/0x14c0 cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0 iterate_dir+0x1c0/0x570 __x64_sys_getdents64+0x133/0x270 do_syscall_64+0x109/0x5d0 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f </TASK>
Allocated by task 83 on cpu 1 at 13.497119s: cifs_buf_get+0x36/0x90 smb_init+0x4f/0x110 CIFSFindNext+0xf7/0x14c0 cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0
Freed by task 83 on cpu 0 at 13.584018s: cifs_buf_release+0x41/0x80 CIFSFindNext+0xfce/0x14c0 cifs_readdir+0xf51/0x29c0
The buggy address is located 16280 bytes inside of freed 16588-byte region [ffff88807c820000, ffff88807c8240cc) ==================================================================
The same memcpy() first reads past the end of that object while it is still live, a slab-out-of-bounds read that the following patches bound; that is the taint the report above carries.
SMB1 is not negotiated by default; reaching this code requires an explicit vers=1.0 mount.
Clear presume_name and resume_name_len whenever a new response is installed and when the rewind path releases the search buffer, so that the name never outlives the buffer it points into, and reset resume_key with them, since it was taken from the same entry and would otherwise be sent with an empty name. A response without a usable last entry then continues the search with an empty resume name rather than a stale one; CIFSFindNext() skips the copy of a zero-length name so that it never runs on the NULL pointer.
The next patch in the series leaves last_entry NULL for a response that carries no entries, and bounds LastNameOffset against the received response rather than against CIFSMaxBufSize. Responses that are given a last entry today then take the path fixed here, so that patch must not be applied without this one.

item.title: CVE-2026-99527 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
spmi: Fix potential use-after-free by grabbing of_node reference
As noticed by Sashiko during a review run of an unrelated patch, in of_spmi_register_devices(), for_each_available_child_of_node() is used to loop through children, and to also assign a node to a newly created SPMI child device.
Problem is that the refcount is dropped at every iteration so, in the specific case of DT overlays, a use-after-free may occur when an overlay is dynamically unloaded!
To resolve this, increase the of_node refcount when assigning (in function of_spmi_register_devices) and release the reference in spmi_device_remove().

item.title: CVE-2026-99528 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
SUNRPC: fix netns use-after-free in write_gssp()
While fuzzing with a customized syzkaller, I hit a refcount warning in xprt_alloc(), reached from a write to /proc/net/rpc/use-gss-proxy:
refcount_t: addition on 0; use-after-free. WARNING: lib/refcount.c:25 at refcount_warn_saturate+0xf8/0x120 CPU: 0 PID: 10404 Comm: syz.0.17 Not tainted 7.3.0-rc1-00096-gcfebfd3db73d Call Trace: <TASK> xprt_alloc+0x83f/0x9d0 xs_setup_xprt+0xaf/0x3c0 xs_setup_local+0x47/0x7f0 xprt_create_transport+0x16c/0x730 rpc_create+0x38e/0x7f0 gssp_rpc_create+0xe2/0x180 set_gssp_clnt+0xba/0x1b0 write_gssp+0x200/0x310 proc_reg_write+0x240/0x330 vfs_write+0x2aa/0x1050 ksys_write+0x12a/0x250 do_syscall_64+0x117/0x750 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f </TASK>
create_use_gss_proxy_proc_entry() stores the struct net pointer as the proc entry's private data without taking a reference on it, and an open file descriptor does not pin the namespace either, as procfs only pins the proc_dir_entry. write_gssp() reads that pointer back with pde_data() and hands it to set_gssp_clnt(), which reaches xprt_init():
xprt->xprt_net = get_net_track(net, &xprt->ns_tracker, GFP_KERNEL);
get_net_track() -> get_net() -> refcount_inc() is unconditional, so rpc_create() assumes its caller holds a reference on args.net. write_gssp() does not.
Dropping the last ns.count reference does not make the file go away. __put_net() only queues cleanup_net() on a workqueue, and the remove_proc_entry() that fences off further writes runs from the rpcsec_gss pernet .exit method, that is, from inside cleanup_net(). A write landing between those two points increments a refcount that is already zero. cleanup_net() does not re-read ns.count, so the namespace is freed anyway and the rpc_xprt -- along with the AF_LOCAL socket opened for it -- is left pointing at freed memory. The resurrected count is visible to the rest of that teardown too: with CONFIG_IPV6_MROUTE the same cleanup_net() worker then trips !mr_can_free_table() in ip6mr_free_table(), which tests check_net() on the namespace it is freeing.
It reduces to opening /proc/net/rpc/use-gss-proxy inside a new network namespace, calling setns() back to the original one to drop the last reference, and then writing "1" to the still-open descriptor.
Take the reference in write_gssp() itself and refuse the write when the namespace is already gone. This is what procfs does for every other /proc/net file: get_proc_net() is maybe_get_net(PDE_NET(PDE(inode))) and seq_open_net() returns -ENXIO when it fails. PDE_NET() cannot be reused here because the parent directory /proc/net/rpc carries no namespace pointer. Adding a .pre_exit to rpcsec_gss_net_ops so the entry is removed earlier would only narrow the window, since pre_exit also runs from cleanup_net().
Live namespaces are unaffected: a write still returns the error from set_gssp_clnt(), a write of "2" still returns -EINVAL, and reads are untouched.

item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
wifi: b43: fix use-after-free in b43_bcma_remove()
b43_one_core_detach() frees the struct b43_wldev it is given the bus device of. b43_bcma_remove() then reads wldev->dev again to free the bus device, which is a read of freed memory.
b43_ssb_remove() does not have the problem: it takes a copy of wldev->dev at the start. Do the same here.

item.title: CVE-2026-99530 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
cgroup: serialize migrations of newly forked processes
With favordynmods enabled, a cgroup.procs migration takes the target threadgroup's cgroup_threadgroup_rwsem for writing. A process fork holds the forking threadgroup's semaphore for reading. These are different semaphores when fork creates a new process.
copy_process() publishes the child's PID before cgroup_post_fork() links the child to its css_set. A writer can find the child in that interval, take its uncontended semaphore, and migrate it while child->cgroups still points to init_css_set and child->cg_list is empty. Migration links the node into init_css_set.mg_tasks. cgroup_post_fork() then adds the same node to the intended css_set as though it were unlinked, corrupting both task lists and their css_set ownership.
This regresses the fork/migration race fixed by commit b12b533fa523 ("cgroups: add lock for child->cgroups in cgroup_post_fork()") and restored again in 2012 after the lock had been removed. The old task_lock protection was later superseded by global css_set and cgroup threadgroup locking. The change identified by the Fixes tag narrowed only the migration side back to a per-threadgroup lock, recreating the different-process exclusion failure.
Take the new threadgroup's semaphore for reading before the child becomes visible and hold it through cgroup_post_fork(). Use a nested lock subclass because fork already holds the parent's semaphore. CLONE_THREAD children share the parent's signal_struct and remain covered by the existing lock. Migrations of unrelated, fully initialized threadgroups remain concurrent.
An AI coding assistant was used to identify and reproduce the regression and to develop and test this fix.

item.title: CVE-2026-99531 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: verify transform SessionId matches the decrypted header
When an encrypted request comes in, the decryption key is picked by the SessionId in the transform header, but the request is then authorized under whatever session the decrypted inner header names. Nothing ever compares the two, so on a connection with more than one session a client can get a request decrypted with one session's key and run it as another session. Encrypted requests are exempt from signing too, so a valid AEAD tag is the only proof of session identity, and it is checked against the wrong session.
MS-SMB2 says the server must check that the transform SessionId matches the one in the decrypted SMB2 header and treat a mismatch as a protocol error. Add that check in __handle_ksmbd_work() after decryption, before dispatching: the message has to be at least one fixed SMB2 header, the first operation must not set SMB2_FLAGS_RELATED_OPERATIONS and its SessionId must match the transform SessionId, and every following non-related operation in a compound chain must carry the same SessionId. NextCommand offsets must be 8-byte aligned and stay inside the message; the bounds check is done by subtraction so it cannot wrap.
When the decrypted payload is a compression transform, the existing decompression step runs first and the decompressed SMB2 message is checked instead, since a compression transform header carries no SessionId.

item.title: CVE-2026-99532 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: validate security descriptor offsets before pointer arithmetic
parse_sec_desc() constructs SID and DACL pointers by adding untrusted 32-bit offsets to the security descriptor before checking their bounds. The existing checks reject offsets into the descriptor header, but do not reject offsets beyond the descriptor's length.
On a 32-bit kernel, a large offset can wrap the pointer before the descriptor. The end-only checks in parse_sid() and parse_dacl() can then accept it, allowing an authenticated SMB2 SET_INFO request to access memory outside the security descriptor and fault the kernel.
Check each nonzero offset against acl_len before constructing its pointer. Initialize the optional owner and group SID pointers to NULL so an omitted SID remains absent when parsing the DACL.

item.title: CVE-2026-99533 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: validate AppInstanceId takeover target
AppInstanceId lookup currently selects the first open with the matching identifier. CREATE for an unrelated share or path can therefore force-close another session's open before authorization of the new target. Matching only the base path also conflates alternate data streams with the unnamed stream.
MS-SMB2 requires the old open to match the share and path, belong to a different ClientGuid, and be closed only when the requester has GENERIC_READ access. Search all opens with the ID and match share, resolved path, stream, and the current connection's client GUID. Retain a share configuration reference in ksmbd_file and reuse its name instead of allocating a name for every open. This keeps matching safe during tree connection teardown and preserves name-based matching across configuration updates.
Refresh the share reference on durable reconnect and restore the old reference if reopening fails. Serialize connection and share comparisons with durable disconnect/reconnect, and recheck the target before closing it. Keep the original ClientGuid for durable replay and lease checks.
Check AppInstanceVersion before querying access, even when GENERIC_READ is absent, and before disconnected delete-on-close cleanup. Rejected CREATE must leave other durable opens untouched. Calculate maximal access on the matched open's referenced path so a rename cannot substitute another file's authorization. Require read access with the effective VFS credentials as well as the NT DACL before takeover. Access denial only skips takeover and leaves CREATE to its normal access checks. Restore filesystem credentials before returning a takeover error.
Handle takeover before checking FILE_CREATE collisions, and re-resolve the path after closing the old open. This lets delete-on-close remove the old file before a new one is created. Include SYNCHRONIZE in the baseline maximal-access mask so read-only files report GENERIC_READ correctly.

item.title: CVE-2026-99534 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: prevent stale data from being written by SMB2 WRITE requests
Initialize the compatibility byte in request buffers without zeroing the entire allocation. Keep the one-byte compatibility exception for SMB2 messages so valid zero-length WRITE requests remain compatible, and validate the data range in the WRITE handlers against the current compound request before accessing it.
This prevents stale request-buffer data from being written to files or sent to IPC pipes.

item.title: CVE-2026-99535 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: prevent share root removal through empty paths
A FileLinkInformation request can supply "/" as the new link name. smb2_get_name() strips the trailing slash and passes an empty string to ksmbd_vfs_kern_path_start_removing().
ksmbd_vfs_path_lookup() resolves an empty pathname as the configured share path, without LOOKUP_BENEATH. With ReplaceIfExists set, smb2_create_link() can therefore remove the share root from its parent before link creation fails. An authenticated client with a writable share and DELETE access to a file can trigger this if the share root is empty and the mapped user has write and search permission on its parent directory.
Return -EINVAL for empty pathnames when for_remove is set, before resolving the share path or acquiring removal resources. Ordinary lookups continue to accept empty pathnames for opening the share root.

item.title: CVE-2026-99536 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: prevent session binding in compound requests
A failed multichannel binding can retain its target session on the work item so that the error response can be signed. Subsequent compound commands can then use that session together with a tree connection left over from an earlier command.
Limit binding SESSION_SETUP requests to standalone messages during message validation, before smb2_sess_setup() can replace work->sess. Check both NextCommand and the current request offset to cover binding in the first, middle and last positions of a compound. The existing validation error path returns STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER and stops processing the remaining commands.
This intentionally limits support for compounded binding. It is not a protocol requirement that binding be standalone. Standalone binding and non-binding compounds retain their existing behavior, without changing session, tree or response encryption handling.

item.title: CVE-2026-99537 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: preserve unreadable named streams on open
A write-only client can open an existing named stream with FILE_OPEN_IF without permission to read the underlying file. The case-insensitive lookup finds the xattr name, but querying its value length then fails with -EACCES. smb2_set_stream_name_xattr() treats every negative result as a missing stream and replaces the existing xattr with an empty value.
A failed xattr list is not proof that the stream is absent either: for example, -ENOMEM can lead to the same empty replacement. Preserve listing errors and create a stream only for -ENOENT or -ENODATA. The latter can occur if the xattr is removed between listing its name and querying its value. Return other lookup errors without changing the stream.
A write-only FILE_OPEN now reports access denied instead of name not found. FILE_OVERWRITE_IF and FILE_SUPERSEDE on an unreadable stream also fail instead of appearing to replace it. Stream writes and EOF changes already need to read the old value, so such handles cannot update the stream after opening either.

item.title: CVE-2026-99538 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: ignore network devices of other namespaces
With no interface list configured, ksmbd binds every interface that comes up. ksmbd_netdev_event() does not look at the device's namespace, and create_socket() opens the listener in the namespace of the task raising NETDEV_UP. A container with its own address on a bridge brings up its interface and finds port 445 in its namespace already taken by ksmbd, so an SMB server running inside the container fails with "Address already in use".
Interfaces are also matched by name only, so a container's eth0 going down would stop the listener on the host's eth0.
Only handle netdev events for devices in init_net.

item.title: CVE-2026-99539 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: fix session reference leak on compounded SESSION_SETUP
A compound request can place SESSION_SETUP after another command. That earlier command leaves a reference to its session in work->sess. smb2_sess_setup() then overwrites work->sess with the session it looks up or creates, and the dispatcher later puts work->sess only once. The inherited reference is never dropped. That leaks the session, together with its setup connection and socket, and every repeat of the compound leaks another.
unreferenced object (size 512): __kmalloc_cache_noprof+0x32c/0x3a0 ksmbd_smb2_session_create+0xf6/0x9c0 [ksmbd] smb2_sess_setup+0xda4/0x6280 [ksmbd] handle_ksmbd_work+0x88c/0x1cb0 [ksmbd]
Save the inherited session on entry. After the request has been processed, release it once, but only when smb2_sess_setup() has replaced work->sess with its own session or cleared it. Do this after ksmbd_conn_unlock() so the put does not run under srv_mutex. An error path may instead leave the inherited session in work->sess. Keep it there, so the dispatcher still puts it and the error response is still signed or encrypted with it as before.

item.title: CVE-2026-99540 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: fix parent dentry lifetime in directory enumeration
ksmbd_populate_dot_dotdot_entries() builds the ".." entry from the open directory's d_parent and passes that pointer to ksmbd_vfs_fill_dentry_attrs() without taking a reference. That pointer is only valid while the directory stays under this parent. If a concurrent rename moves the directory elsewhere, the old parent loses its last reference; a following rmdir then turns it into a negative dentry with d_inode cleared, and after the RCU grace period the dentry itself is freed. The worker still holds the raw pointer and dereferences d_inode through vfs_getattr() and vfs_getxattr().
A remote SMB client, authenticated or guest, triggers this by listing a directory while that directory is moved under a new parent and the old parent is deleted. It can be done by the client itself with write access or by other concurrent writers, triggering null-ptr-deref and slab-use-after-free on a KASAN build.
KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007] Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work RIP: 0010:xattr_permission+0x9d/0x160 Call Trace: vfs_getxattr+0x9c/0x1b0 ksmbd_vfs_getxattr+0x82/0x100 ksmbd_vfs_get_dos_attrib_xattr+0x7f/0x130 ksmbd_vfs_fill_dentry_attrs+0x435/0x650 ksmbd_populate_dot_dotdot_entries+0x25e/0x630 smb2_query_dir+0xcf9/0x1a20 handle_ksmbd_work+0x5f1/0x1c80 process_one_work+0x90b/0x19d0
Fix by using the dentry reference counting APIs: take the parent with dget_parent(), take a matching dget() on ".", and dput() the dentry once ksmbd_vfs_fill_dentry_attrs() has returned or the pattern does not match.

item.title: CVE-2026-99541 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: fix OOB read and cross-share confusion in ksmbd_validate_name_reconnect()
ksmbd_validate_name_reconnect() indexes ab_pathname[share->path_sz + 1] without checking that the path is longer than share->path_sz + 1 (d_path() fills the buffer from the end). A durable fp is not bound to its original share, so a client can preserve a file from a short-path share and reconnect it on a long-path share, making strcmp() read past the PATH_MAX buffer - with a long enough share path this oopses the kernel, and on a mapped page it also gives a byte-equality oracle on adjacent heap (the reconnect succeeds exactly when the out-of-bounds string equals the requested name). A same-share variant with the durable fp at the share root reads 1 byte past the buffer (strlen(ab_pathname) == share->path_sz).
Check before comparing: the path must be longer than share->path_sz, it must start with share->path, and the next character must be '/'. The share root itself is accepted only for an empty name.

item.title: CVE-2026-99542 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: deny access for an empty DACL instead of granting the request
smb_check_perm_dacl() returns the access mask it computes to the SMB2 CREATE handler, which uses it as the granted access for the open. For a security descriptor whose DACL is present but contains no ACEs, the function is supposed to deny access: an empty (non-NULL) DACL grants no access to anyone except the object owner's implicit READ_CONTROL and WRITE_DAC (MS-DTYP 2.4.5).
The empty-DACL branch only denies when both
- the DACL has no trailing bytes (pdacl_size == sizeof(struct smb_acl)), and - the request contains bits beyond READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC.
In every other case it takes the shared "goto err_out" with rc still 0, which returns success without modifying *pdaccess, so the caller grants the full requested access. Three problems follow:
- The READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC carve-out models the owner's implicit rights, but the check runs before is_owner is computed, so those rights are handed to *every* caller, not just the owner. For READ_CONTROL the SMB2 CREATE path does not fall back to inode_permission(), so any user can read the security descriptor of an object whose empty DACL is meant to deny them.
- A request of exactly READ_CONTROL and/or WRITE_DAC is granted to any caller. WRITE_DAC lets the handle rewrite the DACL.
- A DACL that declares zero ACEs but carries trailing bytes (pdacl_size > sizeof(struct smb_acl)) skips the deny entirely and is granted whatever was requested.
On shares where the NT ACL is the authoritative access control -- e.g. "force user" shares, where every client maps to one POSIX identity so POSIX cannot distinguish users -- this is an access-control bypass.
Compute is_owner before the empty-DACL branch and deny access from an empty DACL unless the caller is the owner requesting no more than READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC.

item.title: CVE-2026-99543 - NVD - CVSS: não informado

Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
backlight: qcom-wled: Fix NULL pointer dereference in wled_remove()
wled_probe() doesn't set the driver data for the platform device. As a result, platform_get_drvdata() in wled_remove() will return NULL, and the first dereference of it crashes on unbind.

item.title: CVE-2026-99544 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices
In a CoCo VM the host is untrusted. Since the VMBus ring buffer read and write indices live in shared memory, the guest has to treat both as potentially malicious.
hv_ringbuffer_write() copies into the ring at write_index with no bounds checking, so the host can make the guest write packet data at any offset up to 4 GiB past the start of the ring buffer. read_index matters too: the available space derived from both indices is the only bound on how much is copied, and an out-of-range index can make it far larger than the ring.
The fix is to validate both indices before use and to use the validated snapshot instead of re-accessing. For invalid indices, hv_ringbuffer_write() logs and returns -EIO.
One re-read of write_index is left unchecked in this patch: hv_get_ring_bufferindices() fetches it again for the prev_indices trailer. The value is only returned to the host and is not used as an offset or length for indexing. Since this is not a security issue, it is addressed later in the series.
Open-coding the bytes available arithmetic keeps the fix free of prerequisites; a later patch refactors it into a helper function.

item.title: CVE-2026-99545 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
driver core: take parent lock on deferred probe
USB interfaces should be probed with the parent USB device lock held, but this is not honoured when probe is deferred.
Add a new bus_probe_device_deferred() helper to handle deferred probe where the parent device lock is not held.

item.title: CVE-2026-99546 - NVD - CVSS: não informado
item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
net/sched: cls_flower: avoid stale mask references after delete
Flower releases a mask reference when a filter is removed from the classifier. The filter object can remain alive while dump, walk, or hardware reoffload paths hold a reference to it. Those paths can then dereference f->mask after the mask has already been released.
Keep the mask reference until the filter reference count reaches zero. Release the mask synchronously from the final __fl_put() while the caller still holds the tcf_proto reference, and leave the existing RCU work to free the mask. This keeps the mask available to every reader that still holds the filter.
The filter is still removed from the classifier indexes immediately. Therefore, a deleted filter can temporarily retain an otherwise empty mask; fl_delete() uses the handle IDR, rather than the mask list, to determine whether the classifier has become empty.
Failed mask assignment can leave fnew->mask as an error or borrowed pointer without an owned mask reference. Clear it before the common failure path so the final put cannot release an unowned reference.
This fix does not add fields, snapshots, or per-filter memory.

dm-inlinecrypt ctor # first use of the fallback ├─ blk_crypto_init_key() # succeeds, ctx->key.size != 0 ├─ blk_crypto_start_using_key() │ ├─ hw-wrapped key: -EOPNOTSUPP │ │ # profile never allocated (NULL) │ └─ raw key: fallback_start_using_mode() │ └─ blk_crypto_fallback_init() fails │ └─ kfree(profile) # not NULLed ├─ goto bad └─ inlinecrypt_dtr() # evicts whenever key.size is set └─ blk_crypto_evict_key() └─ blk_crypto_config_supported_natively() = false └─ blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key() └─ __blk_crypto_evict_key(blk_crypto_fallback_profile) └─ profile->num_slots # BOOM!!!
This issue can be reproduced using the following commands:
dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/backing bs=1M count=64 LOOP=$(losetup -f --show /tmp/backing) SZ=$(blockdev --getsz $LOOP) KEY=$(head -c 64 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n') dmsetup create ic --table "0 $SZ inlinecrypt aes-xts-plain64 \ $KEY 0 $LOOP 0 1 keytype:hw-wrapped"
And the following oops is triggered:
================================================================== blk-crypto: loop0: no support for wrapped keys Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc000000000b: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000058-0x000000000000005f] CPU: 5 UID: 0 PID: 901 Comm: dmsetup 7.3.0-rc3 #1 PREEMPT(lazy) RIP: 0010:__blk_crypto_evict_key+0x2e/0x3b0 Call Trace: blk_crypto_evict_key+0x24c/0x320 inlinecrypt_dtr+0xf6/0x160 inlinecrypt_ctr+0x2d3/0xbd0 dm_table_add_target+0x661/0xf40 table_load+0x1c4/0x490 ctl_ioctl+0x32f/0x5f0 dm_ctl_ioctl+0xe/0x20 ==================================================================
dm-inlinecrypt is the only caller that can evict a key that was never started, as fscrypt frees such a key without evicting it.
Fix this by returning early from blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key() when tfms_inited[] is not set for the key's mode. tfms_inited[] is only set after blk_crypto_fallback_init() has successfully initialized the profile, so the crash above is no longer reachable.
The bug has been latent since commit c984ff1423ae ("blk-crypto: dynamically allocate fallback profile") was merged in v6.5, and only became actually triggerable when commit e7f57d2c47e2 ("dm-inlinecrypt: add target for inline block device encryption") was merged in v7.2.

mmap(MAP_HUGETLB) on 32-bit Arm can return an address which is not aligned to the huge page size. In a QEMU virt guest, unmapping the VMA then hits the alignment check in __unmap_hugepage_range():

item.description:
Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
fork: don't create io threads once PF_POSTCOREDUMP is set
zap_process() skips every thread that already has PF_POSTCOREDUMP set. Such a thread is past synchronize_group_exit(), so a coredump can't catch it anymore. It isn't counted in core_state->threads_remaining and it isn't sent SIGKILL.
do_exit() sets PF_POSTCOREDUMP in synchronize_group_exit() and calls io_uring_files_cancel() right after that. The cancellation runs task work and a create_worker_cb() that io-wq queued before the exit creates a new io-wq worker from there. If another thread started a coredump in the meantime that worker joins a thread-group which is already being dumped. zap_process() never saw it so it was never counted. But when it exits it sees signal->core_state in synchronize_group_exit() and decrements threads_remaining like any other thread.
So the count reaches zero one thread early and the dumper leaves coredump_wait_inactive() while a thread it counted is still running.
The task has no fatal signal pending because zap_process() deliberately didn't send it one, and it never went through get_signal() so it doesn't have PF_SIGNALED either.
Refuse to create an io thread when the creator has PF_POSTCOREDUMP. That costs nothing. io_uring_files_cancel() raises IO_WQ_BIT_EXIT before it runs any task work, so a worker created from there only ever gets to exit again, and io_should_retry_thread() doesn't retry -EINTR.
Clearing PF_POSTCOREDUMP for the new thread in copy_process() was the other option. It makes the worker a thread like any other, but it only helps while the dump hasn't started. A worker born after zap_process() has run is invisible to it whatever its flags say and still decrements threads_remaining on the way out. Refusing to create it covers both, and then no task is ever born with the flag, so there is nothing to clear.
Moving io_uring_files_cancel() ahead of synchronize_group_exit() closes the same window. It runs the cancellation, and whatever that can block on, before the thread announces itself to the dumper. A thread that blocks there never reaches coredump_task_exit() at all, so the dumper ends up waiting for a thread that never parks. Refusing the creation leaves the cancellation where it is. But it's very ugly to run io_uring work even before we did all the generic exit work.

Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
smb: smbdirect: release failed pending sockets of a listener
A child of a listener only left the listen.pending or listen.ready list via smbdirect_socket_accept() or when the listener was destroyed. So every connection that failed before it was accepted (negotiate timeout, peer disconnect, invalid negotiate request, ...) stayed on the list and counted against the backlog until the listener was destroyed. After about backlog (10 for ksmbd) such connections smbdirect_listen_connect_request() rejected every new connection with -EBUSY, so an unauthenticated peer was able to permanently stop ksmbd from accepting SMB-Direct connections.
Now a failed child moves itself to a new listen.orphaned list at the end of smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work(), after the disconnect was started, and queues listen.purge_orphaned_work, which releases it with smbdirect_socket_release(), without holding the listener's rdma_lock_handler() lock, in the same way smbdirect_socket_destroy() does for the remaining children. Orphaned sockets still count against the backlog until they are released.
sc->accept.listener is now only changed under listener->listen.lock and whoever clears it is responsible for releasing the socket: smbdirect_socket_accept(), purge_orphaned_work or the destroy of the listener.
In order to make that work:
- a struct smbdirect_socket that is a listener is now freed via kfree_rcu(), so that a child can dereference sc->accept.listener under rcu_read_lock(), even if the listener is released concurrently.
- smbdirect_listen_connect_request() adds nsc to the listen.pending list and sets nsc->accept.listener before it calls smbdirect_accept_connect_request(), and always returns 0 so the rdma_cm core keeps the connection id and nsc owns it. On a non-zero return it schedules nsc's teardown with smbdirect_socket_schedule_cleanup(), which orphans it off the listener so that purge_orphaned_work releases it; nsc destroys its own connection id with rdma_destroy_id() in that teardown. The teardown has to be deferred because the rdma_cm core holds nsc's id_priv->handler_mutex across the handler, so nsc->rdma.cm_id must not be destroyed synchronously from here. That same handler_mutex (and the listener's) also guarantees nsc can't go away under us, so setting the listener before the call is safe and lets a failure orphan nsc.
- smbdirect_accept_negotiate_recv_work() no longer moves a socket to the ready list if it already failed or no longer belongs to the listener. Every accepting socket has a listener, so if sc->accept.listener is already cleared, it no longer sends a negotiate response, as the socket is about to be released.
- smbdirect_socket_destroy() of the listener disables purge_orphaned_work and also releases the orphaned sockets.

Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
smb: smbdirect: don't wait for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync()
smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync() waited for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED after smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work() called rdma_disconnect(). That can take very long, e.g. if the peer just disappeared, until the rdma cm gives up, or forever if the event already happened, but the status was overwritten afterwards.
This is not needed: smbdirect_socket_destroy() drains the qp under rdma_lock_handler(), destroys it and calls rdma_destroy_id(), which only waits for a currently running event handler and makes sure no further events are delivered. The rest of the disconnect protocol (DREQ/DREP and timewait for IB, abrupt close for iWarp) is handled by the rdma core asynchronously. drivers/nvme/host/rdma.c also just calls rdma_disconnect() and ib_drain_qp() before rdma_destroy_id().
So smbdirect_socket_destroy() now also accepts SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTING and changes the status to SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTED itself under rdma_lock_handler().
We could still get RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in the small windows between rdma_unlock_handler() and rdma_destroy_id(), but in that case smbdirect_connection_rdma_event_handler() is basically a no-op.

Thursday 19 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:
ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving another PDU
The receive thread queues a request and can read the next PDU before the negotiation worker finishes. While need_neg is set, the next PDU can cause ksmbd_init_smb_server() to replace conn->ops. A pipelined SMB2 request can therefore make the worker handle an earlier, shorter SMB1 request with SMB2 operations and read beyond its buffer.
An SMB1 multi-protocol negotiate may be followed by an SMB2 NEGOTIATE that changes conn->ops again. Wait for work queued while the connection is new or needs negotiation to complete before reading another PDU. This keeps the operations stable for both stages of negotiation without changing when need_neg is cleared.
